references.text: Joseph sends his brothers away from Egypt, just before their arrival in Canaan.
The brothers loaded the grain onto donkeys and left Egypt, a parallel to the return journey in Gen 45:25.
The brothers return to Jacob in Canaan and tell him what has happened—a strong parallel to the homecoming in Gen 45:25.
Jacob and his entire family travel to Egypt as a direct result of the sons returning with news about Joseph.
Stephen recounts how Joseph sent word and called his father Jacob and all his relatives to Egypt, referring to the events in Genesis 45.
These verses mark the two decisive movements in the patriarchs' history that lead to and from the Egyptian captivity.
Parallel between Jacob's two major return journeys to Canaan after periods abroad.
1 Samuel 12:8 recounts the entire story of decline and restoration as evidence of God's salvation.
The two travel events marking the beginning and end of Jacob's family's time in Egypt.
The departure (Gen 46:5) and the arrival (Gen 45:25) form the two sides of the same historical movement.
Typological parallel: Jesus' flight to and return from Egypt mirrors Israel's history.
